signals.title: USD/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: USD outperforms the G10 basket with a 1W average of +1.180% across 9 pairs, while NOK lags at -0.981% across 2 pairs, generating an extreme 2.161% leader-to-laggard spread. USD/NOK trades at 9.424, clearing its SMA20 at 9.312 while holding below the SMA50 at 9.459 and SMA200 at 9.591. The move is reinforced by policy divergence following the Fed's 4.0% hike relative to Norges Bank at 4.25%, with the Fed's restrictive stance driving broad dollar leadership. Retail positioning displays a strong long bias at 83% long versus 18% short, while NOK domestic data shows severe labor market dislocation with unemployment printing at 4.2% versus 4.6% expected (z = -5.03σ). The wide G10 bilateral divergence reflects persistent greenback capital absorption against commodity and high-beta currencies. Trade bias: Bullish USD/NOK; broad dollar outperformance anchors the upside. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 24 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: G10 spread compresses below 1.20% as oil stabilizes above $101/bbl.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew vs Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 156.13, holding below its daily SMA20 at 156.89, SMA50 at 159.14, and SMA200 at 158.40. Fed 4.0% vs BoJ 1.0% provides a 300bp policy carry advantage for USD, reflected in a +264bp SOFR-TONA OIS spread favoring the dollar. However, Saxo 25d risk reversals show a pronounced put skew of -2.08, signaling substantial institutional demand for downside protection ahead of the BoJ rate decision. Options volatility displays negative VRP with 1M ATM IV at 9.2% versus HV30 at 9.8% (-0.6% premium), reflecting compressed implied pricing relative to realized swings. Leveraged funds net short JPY stands at -53,255 contracts (pctl 30, z -0.53) following a massive WoW short-covering surge of +58,042 contracts. The heavy put skew and aggressive spec covering indicate asymmetric downside risk on any hawkish guidance. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY; severe options put skew caps carry-driven upside into event risk. Catalyst: BoJ Interest Rate Decision ~02:30 UTC — hike bias priced. Risk: BoJ holds rates without hawkish forward guidance, allowing the 300bp carry spread to reassert spot toward 157.00.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long
signals.text: CFTC data shows AUD Leveraged Funds net long at +48,379 contracts (long% 69.6%), sitting at the 93rd percentile of its 52-week range with z = +1.72. The weekly positioning flow reversed with a WoW contraction of -1,871 contracts even as 4-week net added +2,652, highlighting stalling institutional momentum at multi-month extremes. Spot AUD/USD trades at 0.7117, situated below its SMA20 at 0.7170 but holding above the SMA50 at 0.7084 and SMA200 at 0.7013. RBA Governor Bullock stated that upside inflation risks flagged in August are materialising as Middle East tensions escalate, keeping the RBA cash rate at 4.35% versus Fed 4.0% (-35bp spread favoring AUD, with AONIA vs SOFR carry at -73bp). The combination of upper-decile speculative length, stalling weekly flow, and spot failure at the 20-day moving average points to late-trend positioning exhaustion. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish AUD/USD; crowded spec longs constrain upside despite hawkish rhetoric. Catalyst: RBA meeting 29 Sep — hike bias priced. Risk: Clean break above the SMA20 at 0.7170 on re-accelerating weekly leveraged fund inflows.
evidence: RBA 4.35% vs Fed 4.0% — -35bp AUD carry premium

signals.title: GBP/USD — Technical Breakdown + G10 Laggard
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3359, breaking decisively below its moving average cluster where the SMA20 sits at 1.3532, SMA50 at 1.3482, and SMA200 at 1.3455. The pound has weakened across the G10 complex with a 1W average performance of -0.215% across 4 pairs following the BoE holding policy at 3.75%. Fed 4.0% vs BoE 3.75% maintains a 25bp policy rate advantage for USD, while the SONIA-SOFR OIS differential sits tight at -11bp. CFTC speculative positioning reveals vulnerability with GBP Leveraged Funds net long at +40,361 contracts (86th percentile, z = +1.02) despite aggressive liquidations of -7,143 contracts WoW and -2,361 contracts over 4 weeks. Sell-side research notes British Pound futures sliding to late-July lows after the BoE halted long-end gilt sales. The confluence of a technical break below all major daily moving averages and ongoing spec long unwinds leaves the pair vulnerable to further downside. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD; breakdown below the SMA200 accelerates positioning liquidation. Catalyst: UK Retail Sales at 06:00 UTC — forecast 0.9% m/m. Risk: Daily close back above the SMA200 at 1.3455, invalidating the technical breakdown.
